front: Notre start-up vient de lever dix millions d'euros.
pronunciation: [noh-truh star-TUP vyan duh luh-vay dee mee-lyohn duh-ROH]
back: Our start-up has just raised ten million euros.

front: Nous préparons une levée de fonds en série A.
pronunciation: [noo pray-pah-rohn zün luh-vay duh FOHN ahn say-ree AH]
back: We're preparing a Series A funding round.
context: 'Une levée de fonds' = a funding round.

front: La French Tech compte désormais plus de vingt licornes.
pronunciation: [lah frensh TEK kohnt day-zor-meh plü duh van lee-KORN]
back: French Tech now has more than twenty unicorns.
context: 'Une licorne' = a start-up valued at over a billion dollars.

front: Le PDG a présenté le plan stratégique à cinq ans.
pronunciation: [luh pay-day-ZHAY ah pray-zahn-tay luh plahn strah-tay-ZHEEK ah san KAHN]
back: The CEO presented the five-year strategic plan.

front: Le conseil d'administration se réunit chaque trimestre.
pronunciation: [luh kohn-say dad-mee-nees-trah-SYOHN suh ray-ü-nee shak tree-MES-truh]
back: The board of directors meets every quarter.
context: 'Le CA' = the board; 'un administrateur' = a board member.

front: Les actionnaires ont approuvé la fusion.
pronunciation: [lay zak-syoh-NEHR ohn tah-proo-vay lah fü-ZYOHN]
back: The shareholders approved the merger.

front: Le groupe a racheté un concurrent italien.
pronunciation: [luh groop ah rash-tay an kohn-kü-rahn tee-tah-LYAN]
back: The group bought out an Italian competitor.

front: L'entreprise traverse une phase de restructuration.
pronunciation: [lahn-truh-preez trah-vehrs ün fahz duh rus-trük-tü-rah-SYOHN]
back: The company is going through a restructuring phase.
context: Often a euphemism for job cuts.

front: Un plan social prévoit la suppression de cinq cents postes.
pronunciation: [an plahn soh-SYAL pray-vwah lah sü-preh-syohn duh san sahn POST]
back: A redundancy plan provides for cutting five hundred jobs.
context: Officially a 'PSE' (plan de sauvegarde de l'emploi). Strictly regulated in France.

front: Les syndicats ont appelé à la grève.
pronunciation: [lay san-dee-KAH ohn tah-puh-lay ah lah GREV]
back: The unions have called a strike.

front: Le comité social et économique doit être consulté.
pronunciation: [luh koh-mee-tay soh-SYAL ay ay-koh-noh-MEEK dwah teh-truh kohn-sül-TAY]
back: The works council must be consulted.
context: The CSE represents employees in companies with 11+ staff.

front: Nous devons rester compétitifs face à la concurrence chinoise.
pronunciation: [noo duh-vohn res-tay kohm-pay-tee-TEEF fas ah lah kohn-kü-rahns shee-NWAHZ]
back: We need to stay competitive in the face of Chinese competition.

front: Notre cœur de métier, c'est le conseil.
pronunciation: [noh-truh kuhr duh may-TYAY, seh luh kohn-SAY]
back: Our core business is consulting.

front: Il faut diversifier notre portefeuille de clients.
pronunciation: [eel foh dee-vehr-see-fyay noh-truh port-fuhy duh klee-YAHN]
back: We need to diversify our client portfolio.

front: Nous visons une croissance à deux chiffres.
pronunciation: [noo vee-zohn zün krwah-sahns ah duh SHEE-fruh]
back: We're aiming for double-digit growth.

front: Le chiffre d'affaires a progressé de huit pour cent.
pronunciation: [luh shee-fruh dah-FEHR ah proh-greh-say duh wee poor SAHN]
back: Turnover rose by eight percent.
context: 'Le CA' also means 'chiffre d'affaires' (revenue). Context tells you which.

front: La marge opérationnelle s'est dégradée.
pronunciation: [lah marzh oh-pay-rah-syoh-NEL seh day-grah-DAY]
back: The operating margin has deteriorated.

front: Nous devons réduire nos coûts fixes.
pronunciation: [noo duh-vohn ray-dweer noh koo FEEKS]
back: We need to cut our fixed costs.

front: Ce projet n'est pas rentable à court terme.
pronunciation: [suh proh-zheh neh pah rahn-TAH-bluh ah koor TEHRM]
back: This project isn't profitable in the short term.

front: La direction a validé le budget.
pronunciation: [lah dee-rek-syohn ah vah-lee-day luh bü-DZHEH]
back: Management has approved the budget.

front: Il faut aligner toutes les parties prenantes.
pronunciation: [eel foh tah-lee-nyay toot lay par-tee pruh-NAHNT]
back: We need to get all stakeholders aligned.

front: Ce n'est pas dans le périmètre du projet.
pronunciation: [suh neh pah dahn luh pay-ree-MEH-truh dü proh-ZHEH]
back: That's outside the scope of the project.

front: Je vous fais un point d'étape vendredi.
pronunciation: [zhuh voo feh zan pwan day-TAP vahn-druh-DEE]
back: I'll give you a progress update on Friday.

front: Qui pilote ce chantier ?
pronunciation: [kee pee-lot suh shahn-TYAY]
back: Who's running this initiative?
context: Corporate jargon: 'piloter' = to lead; 'un chantier' (building site) = a workstream.

front: Il a été nommé directeur général délégué.
pronunciation: [ee lah ay-tay noh-may dee-rek-tuhr zhay-nay-RAL day-lay-GAY]
back: He was appointed deputy CEO.

front: Elle a gravi les échelons un à un.
pronunciation: [el ah grah-VEE lay zay-shuh-LOHN an nah AN]
back: She climbed the ladder rung by rung.
context: 'Gravir les échelons' = to climb the career ladder.

front: Le plafond de verre existe toujours.
pronunciation: [luh plah-fohn duh VEHR eg-zeest too-ZHOOR]
back: The glass ceiling still exists.
context: Since 2011, French law requires 40% women on large company boards.

front: Un bon manager sait déléguer.
pronunciation: [an bohn mah-nah-ZHUHR seh day-lay-GAY]
back: A good manager knows how to delegate.
context: French uses 'manager' and 'management' freely in business.

front: Il pratique un management très vertical.
pronunciation: [eel prak-teek an man-ahzh-MAHN treh vehr-tee-KAL]
back: His management style is very top-down.
context: French companies are often described as hierarchical.

front: Elle a su fédérer les équipes autour d'un projet commun.
pronunciation: [el ah sü fay-day-ray lay zay-KEEP oh-toor dan proh-zheh koh-MAN]
back: She managed to rally the teams around a common project.

front: Il faut donner du sens au travail de chacun.
pronunciation: [eel foh doh-nay dü SAHNS oh trah-vahy duh shah-KAN]
back: Everyone's work needs to feel meaningful.
context: A popular management theme in France since 2020.

front: La marque employeur attire les jeunes talents.
pronunciation: [lah mark ahm-plwah-YUHR ah-teer lay zhuhn tah-LAHN]
back: The employer brand attracts young talent.

front: Nous misons sur la transformation numérique.
pronunciation: [noo mee-zohn sür lah trahns-for-mah-syohn nü-may-REEK]
back: We're betting on digital transformation.

front: L'intelligence artificielle va bouleverser notre secteur.
pronunciation: [lan-teh-lee-zhahns ar-tee-fee-SYEL vah bool-vehr-say noh-truh sek-TUHR]
back: AI is going to transform our sector.

front: La RSE est devenue un enjeu stratégique.
pronunciation: [lah ehr-es-UH eh duh-vuh-nü an nahn-zhuh strah-tay-ZHEEK]
back: CSR has become a strategic issue.
context: RSE = responsabilité sociétale des entreprises (corporate social responsibility).

front: Notre bilan carbone a baissé de vingt pour cent.
pronunciation: [noh-truh bee-lahn kar-BUN ah beh-say duh van poor SAHN]
back: Our carbon footprint fell by twenty percent.
context: Large French firms must publish their emissions.

front: La gouvernance du groupe a été vivement critiquée.
pronunciation: [lah goo-vehr-NAHNS dü groop ah ay-tay veev-mahn kree-tee-KAY]
back: The group's governance came in for sharp criticism.

front: Il y a un conflit d'intérêts évident.
pronunciation: [eel yah an kohn-flee dan-tay-REH zay-vee-DAHN]
back: There's an obvious conflict of interest.

front: Le lanceur d'alerte est désormais protégé par la loi.
pronunciation: [luh lahn-suhr dah-LEHRT eh day-zor-meh proh-tay-zhay par lah LWAH]
back: Whistleblowers are now protected by law.

front: Le groupe est coté au CAC 40.
pronunciation: [luh groop eh koh-tay oh kak kah-RAHNT]
back: The group is listed on the CAC 40.
context: The Paris stock index of the 40 largest companies.

front: L'action a dévissé après l'annonce.
pronunciation: [lak-SYOHN ah day-vee-say ah-preh lah-NOHNS]
back: The share price plunged after the announcement.
context: 'Dévisser' (to unscrew, or to fall when climbing) = to plummet.

front: La société a été placée en redressement judiciaire.
pronunciation: [lah soh-syay-TAY ah ay-tay plah-say ahn ruh-dres-mahn zhü-dee-SYEHR]
back: The company has been placed in receivership.
context: 'Le redressement judiciaire' = court-supervised recovery; 'la liquidation' = winding up.

front: Le repreneur s'engage à maintenir l'emploi.
pronunciation: [luh ruh-pruh-NUHR sahn-gahzh ah man-tuh-neer lahm-PLWAH]
back: The buyer is committing to preserve jobs.
context: 'Un repreneur' = a buyer of a struggling business.

front: Il faut savoir prendre des risques calculés.
pronunciation: [eel foh sah-vwahr prahn-druh day reesk kal-kü-LAY]
back: You need to know how to take calculated risks.

front: Le leadership, c'est montrer l'exemple.
pronunciation: [luh lee-dehr-SHEEP, seh mohn-tray leg-ZAHN-pluh]
back: Leadership means leading by example.
